1: The process is resolving a customer's billing complaint.
It starts when a complaint lands in the advisor's queue, by phone or web form.
It ends when the customer is told the outcome and the case is closed on the account.
2: A complaints advisor owns the case from start to finish.
A billing analyst confirms whether the charge was correct.
A team leader approves any goodwill credit above the advisor's own limit.
The customer is kept informed throughout.
3: It is triggered when a customer raises a billing complaint.
Roughly forty complaints come in per advisor per day.
It is heaviest just after the monthly bills go out.
4: The inputs are the complaint record and the account's billing history.
The output is a resolution decision, any credit applied, and a closure note on the account.
5: First the advisor reads the complaint in the CRM.
Then the advisor pulls the billing history from the billing platform.
If the charge is wrong, the advisor raises a credit.
If the credit is over their limit, they route it to a team leader for approval.
Finally the advisor calls the customer and closes the case.
6: An advisor can credit up to £25 on their own authority.
Between £25 and £100 needs a team leader's approval.
Between £100 and £500 needs a duty manager.
Anything above £500 goes to the billing governance board.
7: The case record lives in the CRM.
The credit is posted in the billing platform.
A monthly reconciliation is kept in a shared spreadsheet.
8: The advisor uses the CRM for the case and the billing platform for charges and credits.
Outlook is used for internal chasers and the phone system for the outbound call.
10: If the customer has already been credited once for the same issue, it skips straight to a team leader.
If the billing system is down, the case is parked and picked up the next day.
11: About forty cases a day per advisor.
A straightforward case takes about fifteen minutes; a complex one can run over two days waiting on approvals.
The SLA is five working days.
12: Waiting on team-leader approval is the biggest delay; cases can sit for a day in that queue.
People keep their own spreadsheets to track what is pending, and everyone does it slightly differently.
